title: Restricted Assignment Makespan (Polynomial-Time Below 2)
short_statement: In restricted-assignment makespan, each job has a fixed size and a set of allowed machines. The general $2$-approximation applies and the configuration LP estimates the optimum within $\approx 1.94$, but producing an actual schedule below $2$ in polynomial time is open.
open_problem: Find a polynomial-time approximation algorithm with ratio strictly below $2$ for restricted-assignment makespan, or prove that no such polynomial-time algorithm exists under standard assumptions.
background: Restricted assignment is the special case of unrelated-machine makespan where each job has one processing time $p_j$ and can run on a specified subset of machines; it is forbidden elsewhere. This model captures eligibility constraints in scheduling and is much more structured than arbitrary unrelated machines. The general $2$-approximation of Lenstra-Shmoys-Tardos applies, and the problem is hard below $3/2$. Svensson showed that the configuration LP estimates the optimum within $33/17<2$, later improved and simplified by Jansen and Rohwedder to $11/6$. They also gave a quasi-polynomial constructive approximation with that ratio. What remains open is a genuinely polynomial-time algorithm that constructs a schedule with ratio below $2$.
full_statement: In restricted-assignment makespan minimization, there are machines $M$ and jobs $J$. Each job $j$ has a processing time $p_j$ and an eligibility set $M_j\subseteq M$; assigning $j$ to a machine outside $M_j$ is forbidden, equivalently $p_{ij}=\infty$, while assigning it to any eligible machine takes time $p_j$. A schedule assigns every job to one eligible machine and has makespan $\max_{i\in M}\sum_{j\text{ assigned to }i}p_j$. The Lenstra-Shmoys-Tardos rounding gives a polynomial-time factor $2$ approximation even for general unrelated machines. The open restricted-assignment problem is to construct, in polynomial time, a schedule with approximation ratio $2-\varepsilon$ for some absolute $\varepsilon>0$, or to prove that no such algorithm exists under standard assumptions. The problem remains open even though the configuration LP can estimate the optimum below factor $2$ and quasi-polynomial rounding is known.
known_results: The Lenstra-Shmoys-Tardos algorithm gives a polynomial-time $2$-approximation for unrelated-machine makespan and therefore for restricted assignment. The standard hardness barrier is $3/2$: no polynomial-time approximation below $3/2$ exists unless $P=NP$. Svensson proved that, for restricted assignment, the configuration LP has integrality gap at most $33/17\approx1.9412$, so the LP value estimates the optimum below factor $2$. Jansen and Rohwedder simplified and strengthened this analysis to $2-1/6=11/6\approx1.8333$, and their extended work gives a constructive $1.8334$-approximation in quasi-polynomial time. These results leave a precise open issue: sub-$2$ structure is present in the relaxation, but no general polynomial-time algorithm is known to turn it into a schedule. Closing this constructive gap, or proving that it cannot be closed, is the core open problem.

progress.summary: Sub-$2$ LP estimation and quasi-polynomial construction are known. A polynomial-time schedule below $2$ is still open.

counterexample_rationale: LP-gap and local-search obstruction instances are finite, but proving polynomial-time impossibility would require complexity assumptions or reductions.
alphaevolve_rationale: Search can identify bottlenecks in local-search rounding and produce hard eligibility graphs. Proof of polynomial termination or hardness is the key.

literature.synthesis: Restricted assignment lies between graph balancing and full unrelated machines. The configuration LP is strong enough to beat $2$ existentially, unlike the full unrelated case, but the known rounding/local-search arguments have quasi-polynomial or nonconstructive aspects. The challenge is not simply proving a better LP gap; it is turning that structure into a polynomial schedule. This makes the problem a useful test of whether hypergraph matching/local-search ideas can be made efficiently constructive for scheduling.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: Try to polynomially bound the augmenting-tree/local-search depth used in quasi-polynomial rounding. Search for eligibility graphs where local search requires many layers.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: A valid algorithmic resolution must produce a schedule, not merely estimate the optimum or certify feasibility of the configuration LP. The running time must be polynomial in the number of jobs, machines, and encoding length of processing times; quasi-polynomial dependence is not enough for this problem record. The approximation ratio should be measured against the integral optimum. If the claim uses an LP, verify the separation/solving assumptions, the conversion from fractional configurations to integral schedules, and the treatment of large jobs. A lower-bound claim should distinguish NP-hardness of approximation from lower bounds on particular LPs or local-search procedures.

where_posed.text: Constructive gap left by Svensson and Jansen-Rohwedder configuration-LP results for restricted assignment.
where_posed.quote: This is the first quasi-polynomial algorithm for this problem improving on the long-standing approximation rate of 2.
